AI Property Management Tool Development

posts.title: Payment System Project
posts.content:
Right now I’m finalizing an internal payment system for my company (startup media company). I worked solo on this project with Cursor + Claude

## What I did

I built it as a distributed event-based system composed of domain driven microservices.

Key components

- transaction service which functions as the main integration point and orchestrates various transaction types (payments, transfers, wallet deposits, etc) atomically- Abstracts external payment processors like Stripe/Paypal behind a unified interface- Wallet component (Uber style) for managing user balances within our ecosystem (mobile app, web app)

## Tech stack

- Backed services in Node Typescript- Zod for schema validations- Inversify for dependency injection- NextJS for web client- AWS RDS Postgres- AWS EventBridge + SQS- AWS Elastic Container Service- CI/CD GitHub Actions

## Lessons Learned

I think I should’ve used a Monorepo rather than separate repos for each service

- Easier to build shared components- would have allowed me to feed context more easily and leverage AI better

Utilize gRPC for semi-event-based instead of fully event based

- Would have simplified direct dependent requests between services- Reduce latency

NestJS

- I built a template for my backend node services that included inversifyJS for dependency injection, a custom modular file structure, custom annotations for auth guards- My services were flexible and lightweight but I kindve reinvented Nest in my own way 😂

## Would love some feedback

If you’ve built something similar I’d love to hear what patterns/tools/architecture/workflows worked for you guys

posts.title: Bulletproof MCP calls with `available_tools.xml`
posts.content:
sometimes your coding agents don't listen when you want to reference an MCP.

instead of smacking them, give them more context..

it's an XML file called `[available_tools](https://github.com/Vibe-with-AI/ai-sdlc/blob/agentic/.aisdlc/refs/available-tools.xml)`

I made this by copying the relevant pieces of each MCP's [README.md](http://README.md), then asked an LLM to give me the README's into a format including:

- Available tools- description of tools- tool- tool summary- tool description- tool capabilities- tool function- tool function description- tool paramaters

I attached a snippet in the photos, and provided the full file as a GIST.

## Where do I store this?
.ai/refs/

## How do I use this?
I place it in the user guidelines instructing each request that it has MCP's available, and to reference the `./ai/refs/available_tools.xml` for usage details.

## How do I make my own?
Provide the example from [the example](https://github.com/Vibe-with-AI/ai-sdlc/blob/agentic/.aisdlc/refs/available-tools.xml), copy/paste each [README.md](http://README.md) from the MCP you are using, into the `.ai/refs/mcps`, then ask the LLM to use the `available_tools.xml` as a template, and swap it with the contents of the mcp's you plan to use in `.ai/refs/mcps`

Always a message away,
Parker
